newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli hoteliers await recovery in tourism.
newsitem.headline: Israeli hoteliers await recovery in tourism.

text.p: Israeli hoteliers said on Tuesday the country's tourism industry was still in a slump but signs pointed to a recovery later this year.

A survey conducted by the Israel Hotel Association found that most hoteliers expect the decline in incoming tourism, prompted by last year's suicide bombings and West Bank clashes, to continue through the first half of 1997.
But the agreement over Hebron which Israel and the PLO signed in January and hope for progress in peace talks with other Arab partners has had a positive effect, they said.

"Israel today has a more cordial political environment and the reaction is positive but it takes time for this to be translated into increased reservations," said the association's chief economist, Dan Jordan.
He said incoming tourism in January was down 18 percent compared with the same period last year.

Tourism to Israel peaked in the first quarter of 1996, having risen steadily since Israel's landmark 1993 peace deal with the PLO. But a spate of Palestinian suicide bombings that killed 59 people in the Jewish state in February and March snapped the upward trend.
Israeli-Palestinian violence that erupted after the government opened a second entrance to an archaelogical tunnel near Moslem holy sites in East Jerusalem last September also scared visitors away.

Some 2.36 million visitors arrived in Israel in 1996, down seven percent from 1995, the association said. Hotel occupancy rates fell to 65.5 percent on average for the year, compared with 68.1 percent in 1995.
